subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should avatar failure details stay limited to authenticated metadata/UI diagnostics, or should the direct `/avatar/{agentId}` image endpoint return more specific failure statuses such as 413 or 400?
rationale: The remaining behavior sits on an authenticated workspace file-serving route, so clearer feedback improves UX but can change information-disclosure boundaries and the public route contract.

options.title: Use metadata/UI diagnostics
options.body: Keep direct image fetches conservative while using `avatarStatus` and `avatarReason` to show safe missing, oversized, or rejected-avatar guidance in Control UI/WebChat.

options.title: Expose endpoint-specific errors
options.body: Return direct-route statuses such as 413 or 400 only with tests proving no unsafe paths or policy details leak.

options.title: Declare current behavior sufficient
options.body: Close the conflicting PR and this issue as implemented, accepting generic direct-route 404s for rejected local avatar files.

recommendation.title: Use metadata/UI diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches conservative while using `avatarStatus` and `avatarReason` to show safe missing, oversized, or rejected-avatar guidance in Control UI/WebChat.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history owns the avatar feature merge and the later local avatar safety hardening, so they are the best available owner for the route-diagnostics boundary choice.
